policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Salvation, and glory, and power, belong to our God' names glory before power, so δόξα καὶ ἡ δύναμις rather than RP's reversed pair is the text it rendered.
ἔφθειρεν and διέφθειρεν are simple and compound aorists of the same verb, and ASV 'her that corrupted the earth' is identical under either.
ASV 'And a second time they say Hallelujah', with its note 'Greek have said', has a plural subject, so the third-plural εἴρηκαν and not the singular εἴρηκεν is the text it rendered.
The variant is the case governed by ἐπί, and ASV 'God that sitteth on the throne' renders τῷ θρόνῳ and τοῦ θρόνου alike.

The variant is whether αἰνεῖτε takes a dative or an accusative object, and ASV 'Give praise to our God' fits τῷ θεῷ and τὸν θεόν equally, its 'to' belonging to the English idiom rather than to a Greek case.

ASV 'all ye his servants, ye that fear him' sets the two phrases in apposition with no conjunction, and it renders καί as 'and' throughout the verse, so the reading with καί is not the text it rendered.
The variant is the case of the participle, genitive λεγόντων against nominative λέγοντες, and ASV 'saying' is the same for both.
ASV 'for the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigneth' renders the possessive, so κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν and not the shorter reading without ἡμῶν is the text behind this clause.
ἀγαλλιῶμεν and ἀγαλλιώμεθα are active and middle subjunctives of the same verb, both rendered 'let us rejoice' in ASV.
ASV 'and let us give the glory unto him' is hortatory, which tells against the future δώσομεν, but it cannot distinguish the aorist subjunctive δώσωμεν from δῶμεν.
ASV prints 'and' in italics in 'fine linen, bright and pure', marking it as a supply, so the added καί was not in the text it rendered.
The variant is the article τοῦ before Ἰησοῦ alone, and ASV 'the testimony of Jesus' is identical whether or not the Greek has it.

ASV 'he that sat thereon called Faithful and True' must put 'called' before its predicates in English, so πιστὸς καλούμενος and καλούμενος πιστὸς are indistinguishable; its note 'Some ancient authorities omit called' reports an omission that is not among these candidates.
ASV 'And his eyes are a flame of fire', with 'are' italicized as a supply and no 'as' before the predicate, renders the reading without ὡς.
ASV gives only one name in 'and he hath a name written which no one knoweth but he himself', so RP's added ὀνόματα γεγραμμένα καὶ was not in the text it rendered.
ASV 'a garment sprinkled with blood' renders ῥεραντισμένον, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read dipped in' maps βεβαμμένον as the reading it did not follow.
Perfect κέκληται and present καλεῖται both fall together in ASV 'and his name is called The Word of God'.
The variant is the article τὰ alone, and ASV 'the armies which are in heaven' needs a relative clause in English whether or not the Greek has the article.
ASV 'out of his mouth proceedeth a sharp sword' calls the sword sharp and nothing more, so RP's added δίστομος 'two-edged' was not in the text it rendered.
ASV 'I saw an angel standing in the sun' carries the note 'Greek one', which maps ἕνα ἄγγελον, so the reading with ἕνα is the text it rendered.
The readings differ only in whether ἐν stands before the dative φωνῇ, and ASV 'he cried with a loud voice' renders the plain dative and ἐν with the dative alike as 'with'.
Genitive αὐτῶν and accusative αὐτούς after ἐπί are both rendered by ASV 'of them that sit thereon', which marks no difference of case.
ASV 'all men, both free and bond' adds 'both' where the same verse renders the following pair as a bare 'and small and great', so τε καὶ rather than the simple καὶ is the text behind this clause.
The variant is the article τὸν before πόλεμον alone, and ASV 'to make war against him' has no article to place either way.

ASV 'and with him the false prophet that wrought the signs' puts the prepositional phrase before the noun and predicatively, which is the base order μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης and not RP's attributive ὁ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ ψευδοπροφήτης.
The readings differ only in the case of the participial phrase agreeing with λίμνη, and ASV 'the lake of fire that burneth with brimstone' is identical under either.
